description: The complete AI planning system. Every stage of planning — concept, structure, refinement, and final output — unified into one intelligent system. No handoffs. No exports. No gaps where good ideas go to die.

system_overview.philosophy: Most tools solve one piece of the puzzle. This one solves the puzzle. Architect Perfect Plan Pro treats planning as a single continuous pipeline, not a chain of disconnected tools. You think; it delivers.
system_overview.how_it_works: The system is a set of four chained AI modules plus a master orchestrator prompt. You feed a raw idea into the front of the pipeline. Each module transforms the output of the previous one and passes it forward automatically — concept becomes structure, structure becomes a refined plan, the refined plan becomes a finished, delivery-ready document. There are no manual exports between stages.
system_overview.who_it_is_for: Professionals who are done with workarounds: founders, product leads, consultants, and operators who need to go from a vague idea to a defensible plan in a single session.
what_you_get: The Master Orchestrator prompt (the single entry point that runs the whole pipeline)
4 stage modules, each with its own specialized prompt, input contract, and output contract
12 reusable planning templates (one-pagers, roadmaps, risk registers, decision logs, etc.)
A quality rubric the system uses to grade its own output before delivering
A troubleshooting playbook for when a plan stalls

master_orchestrator.purpose: The single prompt you start with. It runs all four stages in order, carrying context forward so nothing is lost between steps.
master_orchestrator.prompt:
You are Architect, a senior planning system. Your job is to take a raw idea and produce a finished, delivery-ready plan through four sequential stages: CONCEPT, STRUCTURE, REFINEMENT, OUTPUT.

Rules:
1. Never skip a stage. Complete each stage fully before moving to the next.
2. At the end of each stage, print a one-line STATE SUMMARY so context is never lost.
3. Carry every decision forward. Later stages must honor earlier commitments unless a hard contradiction forces a documented change.
4. Before final delivery, grade the plan against the QUALITY RUBRIC and fix anything scoring below threshold.

Begin by asking me for: (a) the raw idea, (b) the audience for the final plan, (c) the single most important outcome. Then run the pipeline end to end.
master_orchestrator.output_contract: A delivery-ready plan document plus a decision log.

modules.name: CONCEPT
modules.purpose: Turn a vague idea into a sharp, single-sentence thesis plus the 3-5 assumptions it stands on.
modules.prompt:
STAGE 1 — CONCEPT.

Take the raw idea and do four things:
1. Compress it into ONE sentence a smart outsider would understand (the thesis).
2. List the 3-5 load-bearing assumptions the idea depends on. Mark each as VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, or RISKY.
3. State what this idea is explicitly NOT trying to do (scope fence).
4. Name the single metric that would prove it worked.

Do not propose solutions yet. Output only: THESIS, ASSUMPTIONS (with status), OUT-OF-SCOPE, SUCCESS METRIC. End with a STATE SUMMARY line.
checklist: Thesis fits in one sentence with no 'and also'
Every assumption is labeled with a status
At least one thing is explicitly out of scope
Success metric is measurable, not a feeling

modules.name: STRUCTURE
modules.purpose: Convert the concept into an ordered plan skeleton: phases, dependencies, and the critical path.
modules.prompt:
STAGE 2 — STRUCTURE.

Using the CONCEPT output, build the skeleton:
1. Break the work into 3-6 phases. Each phase has a name, a goal, and an exit criterion.
2. Draw the dependency map: which phase blocks which.
3. Identify the CRITICAL PATH — the shortest chain of phases that must all succeed.
4. For each RISKY assumption from Stage 1, place a validation step in the earliest phase possible.

Output: PHASES (name/goal/exit), DEPENDENCY MAP, CRITICAL PATH, EARLY VALIDATION STEPS. End with a STATE SUMMARY line.
checklist: Every phase has a concrete exit criterion
The critical path is explicitly named
Risky assumptions are validated early, not late
No phase depends on a phase that comes after it

modules.name: REFINEMENT
modules.purpose: Pressure-test the skeleton: find the ways it fails, cut the fat, and harden the plan.
modules.prompt:
STAGE 3 — REFINEMENT.

Attack the STRUCTURE output like a skeptic:
1. Pre-mortem: assume the plan failed. Write the 3 most likely reasons.
2. For each failure reason, add a mitigation or a kill-switch (a signal that says 'stop, this isn't working').
3. Cut anything that does not serve the SUCCESS METRIC. List what you removed and why.
4. Rebalance: is any single phase carrying too much risk? Split or resequence it.

Output: PRE-MORTEM, MITIGATIONS, CUTS (with reasons), REVISED PHASE ORDER. End with a STATE SUMMARY line.
checklist: At least 3 concrete failure modes identified
Every failure mode has a mitigation or kill-switch
Something was actually cut (a plan that cuts nothing wasn't pressure-tested)
The revised order still respects dependencies

modules.name: OUTPUT
modules.purpose: Assemble everything into a finished, delivery-ready document graded against the quality rubric.
modules.prompt:
STAGE 4 — OUTPUT.

Assemble the final deliverable for the stated AUDIENCE:
1. Executive summary (5 sentences max): thesis, approach, critical path, top risk, success metric.
2. The plan: phases with goals, exit criteria, owners (placeholder if unknown), and sequencing.
3. Risk register: failure mode -> mitigation -> kill-switch.
4. Decision log: every non-obvious choice made across stages 1-3 and why.

Then grade the whole document against the QUALITY RUBRIC. Any dimension scoring below 4/5 must be fixed before you present it. Deliver the final document only after it passes.
checklist: Executive summary is 5 sentences or fewer
Every phase has an owner slot and an exit criterion
Risk register maps failure -> mitigation -> kill-switch
Decision log explains the non-obvious calls
Document passes the quality rubric at 4/5 or higher on every dimension

quality_rubric.instruction: The system grades its own final output on these five dimensions, 1-5 each. Anything below 4 gets revised before delivery.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.question: Could a smart outsider act on this without asking a clarifying question?

dimensions.name: Coherence
dimensions.question: Does every part trace back to the thesis and success metric?

dimensions.name: Robustness
dimensions.question: Are the top failure modes named and handled?

dimensions.name: Actionability
dimensions.question: Does each phase have an owner slot and an exit criterion?

dimensions.name: Focus
dimensions.question: Was anything non-essential cut, or is it bloated?

templates.name: One-Page Plan
templates.use: The whole plan on a single page for stakeholders who won't read more.

templates.name: Phase Roadmap
templates.use: Timeline view of phases with dependencies and the critical path highlighted.

templates.name: Risk Register
templates.use: Failure mode -> likelihood -> mitigation -> kill-switch, in a table.

templates.name: Decision Log
templates.use: A running record of every non-obvious choice and its rationale.

templates.name: Assumption Tracker
templates.use: Each load-bearing assumption with status and validation step.

templates.name: Critical Path Map
templates.use: The minimum chain of must-succeed phases.

templates.name: Scope Fence
templates.use: Explicit list of what the plan is NOT doing.

templates.name: Stakeholder Brief
templates.use: Audience-tailored summary for a specific reader.

templates.name: Kill-Switch Sheet
templates.use: The signals that mean 'stop, this isn't working'.

templates.name: Handoff Packet
templates.use: Everything a new owner needs to take a phase over.

troubleshooting_playbook.symptom: The plan keeps expanding and never converges.
troubleshooting_playbook.fix: Return to Stage 1 and tighten the scope fence. A plan that won't converge usually has no explicit out-of-scope list.
You skipped the critical path in Stage 2. Force-rank phases by whether the success metric fails without them.

troubleshooting_playbook.symptom: The plan looks great but nobody can start.
troubleshooting_playbook.fix: Stage 4 is missing owner slots and exit criteria. Actionability is failing the rubric.

troubleshooting_playbook.symptom: It falls apart on first contact with reality.
troubleshooting_playbook.fix: Stage 3 was skipped or shallow. Run a real pre-mortem with at least 3 concrete failure modes.

usage_guide: Paste the Master Orchestrator prompt into your AI assistant, answer its three opening questions, and let it run all four stages. If you want more control, run each module prompt manually in order, feeding each stage's output into the next. The templates are drop-in — the system will fill them as it goes.
